messages.subject: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.subject_clean: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am interested in a region on human chromosome 11 (47,371,468 bp to 47,441,229 bp, length 69,762 bp). I have total RNA sequencing data on 500 individuals which have been aligned to the genome using STAR. There are very few annotated features in this region (four). I would like to know how many reads align to this region. How can I determine this, using the output files generated by STAR (sam.bam files)? Is there any way to use the featureCounts function?
Thanks, Ina

messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.subject_clean: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.body_plain:
Yes, featureCounts can do it. Since you already have had the mapping results (ie the sam and/or bam files), and you have defined the target region (chr11, 47,371,468 bp to 47,441,229), you can first create a SAF format annotation file that contains only one line:

target chr11 47371468 47441229 +

, where the delimiter is <TAB>. Let's say the file name is my_annotation.SAF .

You can then run featureCounts like

$ featureCounts -a my_annotation.SAF -F SAF -o my_counts.txt -p -T 8 *.sam *.bam

This will generate a new file, my_counts.txt. If there are 500 individuals, I assume that you have 500 sam or bam files, so you will have 500 columns (plus 6 columns defining the target region) in this file, giving the counts of read-pairs in each sam or bam file that are mapped to the target region.

Can you upgrade to the latest version of Rsubread (1.34.6) to see if it solves the problem?

I also noticed that you used both "annot.inbuit" and "annot.ext" options. This wouldn't end up with errors, but it made featureCounts ignored the "annot.inbuilt" option. You may run featureCounts() twice, one with the "annot.inbuilt" option and the other with "annot.ext".

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject_clean: featureCounts v1.6.5 BAM file SE/PE reads mixture
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
since version 1.6.5 featureCounts supports read counting from BAM files containing both SE and PE reads. I have some mixed BAM files and ran the new version on them. I noticed that if one sets the -s parameter to 0 (unstranded) then both SE and PE are counted, but if you set this parameter to 1 or 2 (stranded or reversed stranded) then SE are excluded and therefore not counted.
Would it be possible to treat the SE reads as unstranded and count them while counting the PE reads as stranded/reversed as defined by parameter -s? Thanks in advance.

Kind regards,
Paul

messages.subject: Re: error reading CRAM file with featureCounts
messages.subject_clean: error reading CRAM file with featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
No, featureCounts in its current version doesn't support CRAM-format input files.  It can only read SAM or BAM files as read mapping results.

You may need to convert the CRAM files into SAM/BAM files before running featureCounts.
